element_notes: 'keywords' define the overall DFT setup (functional, job type, SCF/grid settings, and relativistic options). For transition-metal complexes, consider using a scalar-relativistic treatment when appropriate.
'basis' specifies the basis sets used in the calculation. Basis sets can be assigned per element/atom and should be consistent with the chosen methodological setup.

'cpcm' refers to the CPCM solvation keywords. In newer ORCA versions, the recommended solvation models are CPCM and/or SMD; set the dielectric constant (epsilon) and other relevant solvent parameters accordingly.
'rel' refers to the relativistic options. For Cu complexes, it is common to use scalar-relativistic treatment (e.g., ZORA/DKH) for the d-electrons.
'scf' refers to the SCF settings. For high band-gap complexes, using less tight SCF convergence thresholds can help improve SCF convergence.
'method' defines special methods, theories, or basis-set-related settings that are important for the calculation and require special attention.
'geometry' defines the molecular structure corresponding to a ceramics cluster complex that includes Mn, Ca, O, C, N, and H elements.
